model_interpretation.claim: The measured parent using four rows per CTA through padded width 1024 and two rows for wider inputs was correctness-valid with a 42.64 µs mean. This establishes a useful grouped baseline, not that its mapping beats T1.
model_interpretation.applicability: Grouped multi-row softmax follow-up experiments; this does not compare against T1.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Measure the narrow-width eight-row variant against the parent and retrieve T1's best measured direct one-row result for a compatible comparison.

model_interpretation.claim: For padded widths up to 128, assigning eight complete rows to a CTA instead of the parent's four may reduce CTA scheduling overhead while adding little per-row column state. Keep the parent's four-row mapping at intermediate widths and two-row mapping for wider rows to limit per-CTA work; the larger small-width group could still hurt occupancy. The supplied parent was correct at 42.64 µs mean, versus the 211.984 µs baseline, but these measurements do not establish a win over T1.

model_interpretation.claim: Grouping four complete rows per CTA for widths up to 1024, and two rows with eight warps for wider rows, may reduce CTA scheduling overhead while keeping per-thread work bounded for the wider case. A masked power-of-two column tile and per-row max-subtracted FP32 reductions preserve tail handling and stable softmax; grouping can still hurt occupancy or increase resource use, so the controller must measure it.

items.subject: Grouped multi-row-per-CTA kernel
items.objective: Test CTAs that compute multiple independent complete rows using per-row reductions. Explore rows-per-CTA and only the layout/warp choices needed for this grouped mapping; do not repeat T1’s one-row configuration search or use streaming or split-row algorithms. Compare against T1’s best measured direct one-row result and the official candidates. Support arbitrary valid shapes and tails and preserve the stated accuracy and input/output requirements.
